    Lemma 8.21(2): the primitive return corner is cyclic Nakayama #

    primitive-ray-equations.tex (lem:primitive-cyclic-corners(2)): "the full corner S_x … is a cyclic Nakayama algebra. … List them as y_1, …, y_t. The comparison maps satisfy f_i h_{ij} = f_j, h_{ij} h_j = h_i, h_{ji} = h_j f_i. … Hence the full corner is generated by the cycle x → y_1 → ⋯ → y_t → x. Every simple forward or wraparound path is a generating ray, and full cycles are the local generators. All rays are these paths times powers of a full cycle; the only relations are zero paths."

    We list the return partners y_1, …, y_t of x by the degrees of their generating rays f_i : x → y_i (a chain under factorization, partner_chain), take the cycle arrows x → y_1 → ⋯ → y_t → x (f_1, the comparison maps, the reverse h_t), and show: full cycles are the local generators, consecutive paths between distinct vertices of S_x are its generating rays (by degrees), and every nonidentity ray of S_x is a consecutive path (cyclicNakayama). Consecutive products are cpath a i ℓ = a_i a_{i+1} ⋯ a_{i+ℓ-1}.

          theorem MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.RaySys.Sys.cyclicNakayama {V R L : Type} [AddCommGroup L] [DecidableEq L] [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R] (S : Sys V R L) (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (hfin : IsRepresentationFinite k ↥(S.P.Lin k)) {x : V} (hqx : S.q x ≠ 0) :
          ∃ (n : ℕ) (σ : ℕ → V) (a : ℕ → R), σ 0 = x ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ), σ (m + (n + 1)) = σ m) ∧ Set.InjOn σ (Set.Iio (n + 1)) ∧ (∀ (v : V), S.InS x v ↔ ∃ i < n + 1, σ i = v) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ), S.P.src (a m) = σ m ∧ S.P.tgt (a m) = σ (m + 1)) ∧ (∀ (i : ℕ), S.cpath a i (n + 1) = S.q (σ i)) ∧ ∀ (r : R), S.InS x (S.P.src r) → S.InS x (S.P.tgt r) → r ≠ S.P.e (S.P.src r) → ∃ (m : ℕ) (ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ ℓ ∧ S.rr r = S.cpath a m ℓ

          Lemma 8.21(2) (lem:primitive-cyclic-corners(2)): the primitive return corner S_x is a cyclic Nakayama algebra. Its vertices are σ_0 = x, σ_1, …, σ_t (the return partners, in the order of the chain of their generating rays), the arrows a_i : σ_i → σ_{i+1} (indices mod t + 1) form a cycle, each full cycle is the local generator, and every nonidentity ray between vertices of S_x is a consecutive path a_m a_{m+1} ⋯ a_{m+ℓ-1}; products of rays are thus concatenations, and the only relations are zero paths.
